The Spell announces the kill, and Sunny's fragments rise to 307 of 1000. But the Stone Saint's count is still 6/200, so kills made by Shadows benefit the master and not the Shadow. Consuming Memories is the only way to feed her, which complicates things.

With his experiment finished, Sunny has nothing much to do. He could hunt with the Stone Saint and bathe the ruins in monster blood, but he does not trust himself to stay cautious once easy wins pile up, so he decides to proceed slowly. He has a hobby: exploring the ruins. He loved finding the Vile Thieving Bird's nest and enjoys piecing together fragments of the city's past, maybe a trait inherited from Teacher Julius. He is especially curious about the young priestess whose quarters became his lair. His latest project is the ruins of a grand library. None of the books survived, but the people liked stone engravings. A huge fresco covers the floor of the main hall, buried under rubble too heavy for him to lift, though the Shadow Saint might manage it.

He carves meat and soul shards from the dead centurion and remembers that the spot marked on the crude map from the thug's body is not far away. He tells himself the map is fake, or something awful is there, but curiosity wins. Few Nightmare Creatures hunt in this remote part of the city, as if something compels them to avoid it. With the Stone Saint hiding in his shadow, he feels braver.

In a dark courtyard of a once-magnificent building he finds a well covered by an enormous ornate iron grate. He drops a stone through it and hears nothing. Then a melodic, enchanting voice speaks from below: 'Ah, a guest…' Sunny staggers back, then forces himself to stay. The voice adds that it has not been fed in a long, long time.

The voice from the well echoes in whispers and sounds like a young man's, smooth and charming. Sunny is covered in cold sweat. He has met only one other creature that mimicked human speech, the thing from the dark sea that came in a mantle of fog and stole Cassie's voice. He survived that only because she warned him to keep his eyes shut. He wonders why the hunters were looking for such a horror, and decides to stay and find out, since he has to warn Nephis if something is brewing in the castle. He is grateful for the heavy grate and prepares to summon the Stone Saint and the Midnight Shard.

He says it is nice to meet the voice. It answers that the pleasure is its own, and Sunny thinks of fairy tales about monsters that play riddles with lost children. Then the voice complains that his captors have been tardy, saying it has been alone for three days, and jokes that starvation is their best idea yet because it will help his BMI as a trainee preparing to debut. Sunny is dumbfounded, and realizes that if the hunters were bringing food to a prisoner, that would explain the skipped meals.

He asks who the voice is. The voice realizes he is not one of its captors and so must be a Nightmare Creature, and panics, saying he has only heard of one other creature that mimics human speech. Sunny finds the voice beautiful even in despair and tries to remember the task. His shadow is bent over, holding its stomach, shoulders shaking with laughter.

Sunny understands how bad things look from inside the well. He has never been good at talking to people and three months alone has made it worse, so he asks what Cassie would say and awkwardly declares that they are both humans. The man laughs and says he does not believe him, still using honorifics in case he is an elder monster. Sunny explains that his Aspect lets him walk in the dark and see through it. The man says thugs tried to shake him down for his Memories, he refused, and they have kept him in the well for a couple of weeks, trying clumsy methods to make him transfer them. Sunny thinks it is just tiresome human business, so no danger to Nephis and Cassie, and starts to leave.

The man begs him to come back and offers half his fortune to get him out, saying he has a stash of soul shards in the castle, at least ten. Sunny does not need the shards, but a person with lots of shards and a debt to him would make a perfect proxy for buying Memories without drawing attention. He asks if people know the man is rich, and the man says yes, since he is known to spend heavily on entertainment and arts.

Sunny worries he cannot get him out of such a deep well and that the Prowling Thorn's string is too short. He asks his name, and the man answers Kai. Sunny says that unless Kai can fly, he cannot help. After a long silence, Kai says, 'I can. That's my Aspect Ability.'

Sunny considers Kai's Ability. Flying is rare, and on the Forgotten Shore, where darkness floods the world every night, it is priceless. It explains the soul shards, and why his captors were gentle in trying to force out his Memories, since he was worth more alive. Sunny agrees to open the grate, but says he does not need the shards. Instead, Kai must do something for him, which will be errands inside the castle. He adds that if Kai breaks the deal and flies away, he will find and kill him, which is a fact, not a threat. Kai accepts, sounding resigned.

The Stone Saint comes out of the shadows and slides the heavy grate aside, while Sunny waits with the Midnight Shard drawn. Nothing happens, and Kai explains that all six of his captors needed to put it in place, so he asks how Sunny moved it alone. Sunny reluctantly admits to having a very strong Echo. Kai says very few people in the castle have Echoes and asks his name. Sunny says Sunless, and Kai laughs that it does not sound like a soul-devouring demon, then notes that no one in the castle has that name. He asks if Sunny lives in the outer settlement, and Sunny's Flaw forces him to say no. Kai sums him up as someone who walks the ruins alone at night, has the strength of six men, and calls himself Sunless. Sunny answers that he would climb out, because he can put the grate back anytime, and orders the Saint to move it. Kai stops him and agrees to come out, if Sunny is not a demon.

A breeze rises from the well and a graceful figure floats up and lands in front of it. Kai is human, a young man in light lamellar armor of burnished brown leather over deep blue embroidered garments, with luscious dark auburn hair and mesmerizing green eyes. He is also drop-dead gorgeous, with an ivory complexion and warm charm, and he even looks kind. Sunny finds it a cruel injustice, and notes that two weeks in a pit did nothing to lessen his glamour.

Kai sees the Shadow Saint's burning ruby eyes in the dark and recoils, thinking it is a demon after all. Sunny says he is behind him, and Kai spins around, one hand ready to summon a weapon. Sunny assures him that the Echo is the demon-looking one, not him. Kai asks if he is really human, and Sunny suggests he summon light to check. Kai asks if it will attract monsters, and Sunny says it is secluded, which is probably why the thugs chose it. Kai summons a paper lantern. Sunny pretends to be blinded to make him feel safer.

Kai sees that he is human, and says he is a cutie, which offends Sunny. He asks where Sunny lives and recognizes him as the crazy kid who lives alone in the ruins. Sunny says to call him Sunny, then teases Kai with true statements about his talking rock and his shadow's opinions. Kai pales, and Sunny says he is joking, adding darkly that he cannot stand the rock and barely talks to the shadow.

Sunny is annoyed by how good-looking Kai is, and is also out of practice talking to people, so he treats the joke as training for the castle. Kai stares at him strangely, then explains that his Flaw is that he can tell when someone is lying. So he knew right away that the part about a talking rock was true. Sunny is furious that a lie detector is a Flaw, and realizes it counters half his tricks. He explains that the talking rock is a Memory that repeats words and works as an alarm, and that his shadow has some personality because of his Aspect. When he asks why Kai made him spend half an hour convincing him, Kai answers that he did not know if his Flaw works on Nightmare Creatures.

Kai agrees to keep his promise and asks if they should go to the castle together. Sunny says not yet and tells him to fly to the big ruined cathedral to the south and wait on the roof, since Sunny cannot travel with a lantern. He warns him not to go inside, because a Fallen Devil there butchered the thugs who kidnapped him. Kai is shocked that they are dead, then thanks Sunny, repeating that he never breaks a promise. He flies off, with only his paper lantern visible like a lonely star.

Sunny trembles. He whispers the words of Cassie's prophecy about a lonely star burning in the black sky while the castle burns with rivers of blood in its halls. For a moment he thinks it refers to Kai, but he knows the truth of the prophecy, and he asks his shadow if it is already starting. It has been since they entered the ruined city.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 119: A Fistful of Soul Shards
chapters.chapter_summary:
With dawn approaching, Sunny makes his way back to the cathedral through shadows, since night monsters grow restless, and many of them can perceive things in the dark. He climbs onto the roof and finds Kai standing nervously with a horn longbow, staring into the darkness. To avoid an arrow in the face, he announces himself. Kai whispers that the Fallen Devil might hear them, and when Sunny says it will not, Kai believes him at once. Sunny realizes that since Kai can tell when someone lies and Sunny cannot lie, Kai can take everything he says as true.

Sunny says he will go into the hole on the roof to retrieve something and tells Kai to wait. Kai asks about the devil, and Sunny says he hides well, and fantasizes about killing the bastard someday. He learned the limits of his concealment from the Black Knight, which left him with his insides outside. Kai says it is an awesome Ability, and that he wishes he had it, and Sunny asks if he is tired of being ogled by supermodels. Kai asks how he guessed.

In his lair, Sunny takes off his monster-skin rucksack, puts the centurion meat on the silver plate, and fills the rucksack with half his soul shards, enough to drive people to murder. He does not want to go near the castle, and the thought makes him want to stay in his dark room forever, but he must buy Memories to strengthen the Shadow. He tells himself Kai will do all the work, shuts the rucksack so no light shows, and leaves without looking back, headed for the castle and the memories he left there.

In the light of dawn, Sunny and Kai cross the ruins. The thousands-of-years-old city walls hold back the black sea, and Sunny finds the distant Crimson Spire ominous. He picks a meandering route around the lairs of dangerous creatures, with Kai following with his bow ready. Sunny raises a hand and tells him to listen. A sound like a woman weeping drifts through the fog, and Kai asks hopefully if it could be a human girl. Sunny says the chances are low, and they hide behind a rubble pile.

Sunny sends his shadow to climb a building and look, which bewilders Kai. He asks where Kai's arrows are, and Kai says his specially crafted quiver was taken by the men who put him in the well. His bow is not useless, because he also has arrow-type Memories, but only two, and Sunny says that is not enough. The shadow sees a four-legged beast with rotten, emaciated flesh, white ribs showing through the holes, and a partially bared dog-like skull, which is one of the Fallen. It lets out a human-like sob and waits for a reply. It is not on their path and will pass.

With ten minutes to wait, Sunny summons the Endless Spring and drinks, then lets Kai drink, since he has had no water for two or three days. Kai asks if Sunny arrived at the last solstice, then excitedly asks what the top music video on the charts is. Sunny has no idea, and Kai smiles and asks another question.

For ten minutes Kai peppers Sunny with questions about shoes in fashion, celebrity scandals, award ceremonies, and the latest dance craze, none of which Sunny can answer. Kai finally asks whether he was a hikikomori in the real world, and Sunny does not know the word, saying he once lived in a cargo container. Kai says he has been stuck on the Shore for two and a half years and that life here is monotone. Surprised that such a person has survived that long, Sunny suspects he is part of Gunlaug's gang. Kai says he despises bullies like Gunlaug and calls the king's armor hideous, but admits he takes jobs from Gunlaug's lieutenants, which is why Gunlaug tolerates him. Sunny believes him, and concludes that anyone who dared kidnap Kai could not have been one of the untouchable cohort.

They continue to the center of the city. The castle stands on a tall hill, with dozens of towers, gargoyles, and a narrow fortified road, ending at a staircase and a former muster ground that is now a slum of shabby buildings. People greet Kai as Night, and he says he is known as Nightingale. Sunny notices that people seem more energized and confident than before, with a tense air, and thinks that she was busy these three months too.

He asks Kai to enter the castle and find out who is selling Memories and for how much, and waits in an alley. Hours pass without trouble, until a painfully familiar voice behind him says, 'Hi, Sunny.' He turns and forces a smile: 'Hey, Neph. Long time no see.'

Nephis has changed. She still wears the Starlight Legion Armor, with a white cloak added, and her silver hair now nearly reaches her shoulders, which makes her look mature and feminine. The veil of detached indifference seems cracked, and she seems more alive and resolute, with the power of conviction. Sunny both longs to see her and hoped never to, and she is the real reason he left the castle.

A flashback follows, four months earlier. After the escape in the boat of demon bones, Sunny wakes Cassie as the sky lightens in the east. The three are perched on a giant stone hand that rises from the black waves, and Nephis lies unconscious in the center of the palm with her armor shattered. They have escaped the Soul Devourer, the darkness, and a battle with the creature of the depths. Sunny sleeps, and when he wakes the sun is high. Blood Weave has kept his injuries, even the broken finger, from being as painful as he expected. Cassie has covered Nephis with her cloak. He remembers her flesh restoring itself in the purifying flame and wonders why she never used it to heal herself before.

Looking around, he sees the western edge of the crater and understands they almost crossed it. Behind him he sees a wall in the distance, and tells Cassie that they have found the city she saw. Nephis stays unconscious for two days. On the third she wakes, flat and distant as before, and asks why Sunny is smiling. He tells her to look behind her. She sees a tall grey wall of polished stone above the slope of the crater, a sign of hope.

Once Nephis recovers, they leave the stone hand, planning to cross the crater and climb the wall before sunset. As before, Sunny and Nephis take turns climbing down a few dozen meters and lowering Cassie with the golden rope. They are far stronger than when they climbed down the statue, thanks to two months of fighting in the Labyrinth. Sunny thinks he would be counted among the elite of his generation once back in the real world, which could be a problem. But he can blame everything on Nephis, the last daughter of the Immortal Flame clan, who received a True Name in the First Nightmare and was top of her Academy batch. People will believe she carried two weaklings to the Gateway, and he is a master at choosing words.

Nephis tells him to stay vigilant, and Sunny knows the last stretch is often the most dangerous. Looking back, he sees the statue whose hand sheltered them: a slender woman in a flowing robe with arms raised to the sky, one broken off, with seven stars carved on her robe, and, like the knight, no head. He remembers Cassie's vision of seven severed heads guarding seven seals, and decides he will never come back to the Forgotten Shore.

Near the almost-vertical slope, a stone he is about to step on rolls away and roars. It is a monster, with a mouth full of sharp teeth, and it clamps onto his shin. The Puppeteer's Shroud's boot is too tough, and it just chews on the leather. Nephis looks amused. Sunny wraps the Midnight Shard in shadow and shatters it. The Spell announces he has slain an awakened monster, a Rolling Stone, and that he has received a Memory, which he says is an ordinary rock.

The three stand beneath the city wall, which is made of massive slabs of grey granite, wet and almost black, and at least sixty meters high, twice the height of the Academy's defense barrier. Sunny wonders who built it and what fate befell them, then tells himself the mysteries are no longer his problem. They decide it is easier to climb than circle in search of a gate that may not open. Using the golden rope and, where there are no holds, their swords in the joints between slabs, they climb the wall, aided by strong bodies from the consumed soul shards, shadow fragments, and constant fighting.

On top, Sunny crawls forward and looks down. Beneath is an expansive city in ruins, with shattered stone buildings, many blackened by fire and scarred with claw marks, and the bones of ancient horrors protruding from the ground. Nothing human walks the streets, but the ruins are teeming with Nightmare Creatures. He describes it to Cassie, repeating her vision's words: a vast ruined city of weathered stone, with monsters in its streets. The wall is as wide as a road and encloses the ruins in a perfect circle, with towers built into it.

His eyes are drawn to a tall hill with a magnificent castle of radiant white stone with towers and spires, which he describes as untouched by darkness, and Cassie says it is the castle she saw. But looking behind it, he sees the silhouette of a cyclopean tower like a spear of solidified blood, the Crimson Spire, which fills him with fear. Nephis stares at it too, with a dark expression, then composes herself and says the last stretch may be extremely dangerous, so they must not hurry and should find a way down first.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 125: A Feast in Time of Plague
chapters.chapter_summary:
Neither Nephis nor Sunny wants to descend from the wall, which would cut off their retreat, so they follow it north toward the nearest tower. Nothing seems interested in scaling it, but Sunny keeps shivering at the Crimson Spire and consoles himself that they will soon be out. The round tower rises a dozen meters above the wall, with a broken wooden gate opening into darkness.

Cassie stops them, saying 'Listen.' From inside comes a sound of chomping, crunching, and tearing flesh. Sunny sends his shadow in. It finds several monsters, cut apart as if by an enthusiastic butcher, a large pile of gnawed bones, and a fire in a ring of stones with skewers of monster meat roasting. Beside it sits a young woman a little older than they are, tall and attractive, with hazel eyes and brown hair in a braid. She has an extremely athletic build with lean muscle, dewy olive skin, and a short white tunic with bronze greaves, vambraces, and a cuirass with leather pteruges. She radiates vitality.

Strangest of all, she looks completely relaxed and happy. In months on the Shore, Sunny has never lowered his guard completely, nor have Nephis or Cassie, even under the Soul Devourer's hex, but she seems content, happier than he has ever been. She devours the meat messily. Sunny returns to his body and tells Nephis it is either a very hungry human girl or a very gluttonous demon.

Nephis tells Cassie to follow behind and the three approach the tower, knowing there are two outcomes: the stranger is a local Awakened who will guide them to the nearest human Citadel, as is customary, or she is a Nightmare Creature and they have a hard fight. Inside, the smell of roasting meat makes Sunny's stomach growl, and a bone flies past his head and shatters on the wall. The woman has noticed them, and grins, murmuring in human language: 'Why don't you come out to play…' Sunny and Nephis dismiss their swords and step into the firelight.

She is considerably taller than Nephis and Sunny, with olive skin and archaic armor, like an ancient goddess. She invites them to sit, and when Nephis tensely asks if she is human, she asks what else she could be, a horse, and laughs. She hears that they have just reached the city after two months in the Labyrinth and whistles with respect. Nephis introduces herself, Cassia, and Sunless. The woman says her name is Effie and that she is a Sleeper too, which surprises Sunny, who does not remember her from the Academy. He asks if she is from the castle, and she says yes, with something like pity in her eyes.

She offers to take them there and asks if they have shards. They show the two they took from the Rolling Stone, and she tells them to keep them. When Nephis asks how long it will take to reach the Citadel and Gateway, Effie bursts into hysterical laughter. Then she says she can take them to the castle, but there is no Gateway there and no way out of this hell at all. She has been stuck for three years. 'Welcome to the Dark City.'

Sunny feels something precious shatter in his chest. Cassie asks what Effie means, and Effie says that the Forgotten Shore is not a place where humans are meant to survive, which is why no school or Academy ever mentioned it. Sunny realizes that if no one ever returned to tell others about the Shore, that would explain why such a unique region is unknown, and blames himself for not seeing it when neither Nephis nor Cassie managed what he could not. Effie explains that about fifteen years ago a group of powerful, desperate Sleepers reached the city and claimed the castle, not for a Gateway but because it was the only safe place, and that a few people find their way there each solstice, only to get stuck.

Nephis sits with clenched fists, and Cassie, whose vision led them here, is deathly pale and says it is not fair. Effie says that nothing is ever fair. Then she cheers up, saying the three of them are lucky to have met her. The Dark City is the safest place on the Shore, since no sea monster can cross the wall, and also the deadliest, because nearly every Nightmare Creature in it is Fallen rank. Sunny shudders at the shapes he saw moving in the ruins. Effie says that without an experienced hunter like her, they would have been feasting material before they got down from the wall, and offers them meat.

Nephis asks why no one has left. Effie says there is nothing but coral and sea for months in every direction, no way to cross on foot or swim, and swarms of flying horrors in the clouds. Many tried, and the castle's first master died that way. When Sunny asks if they just hide in the castle and wait for death, she laughs and says most cannot even get in, because the king demands a tax.

Effie explains that the castle belongs to a man named Gunlaug. To live inside its walls, protected and provided for by his hunters, a person must pay one soul shard a week. Those who cannot are banned from the gates and live in a settlement below, trembling at night. Sunny feels a familiar dark feeling return. Shards come from hunting awakened creatures without stumbling into something deadlier. Gunlaug's people form parties led by pathfinders and bring back food, Memories, materials, and shards, and anyone can try the same, though without good Memories and knowledge of the city they usually die. Effie claims she has survived a hundred or two hundred hunts alone, which impresses Sunny. When he asks why she does not just pay the tribute, she says she does not like the ambiance there.

Nephis asks about other ways to earn shards. Effie says a useful Utility Ability can make someone a craftsman or artifex, who are well cared for. Otherwise, boys can become Gunlaug's soldiers, while girls can enter his harem, especially pretty ones, and no one forces anyone. Nephis, with white sparks in her eyes, says the choices are soldier, servant, plaything, or death. She asks why no one has killed him. Effie says many have tried, and their skulls hang above the castle gate, and that Gunlaug is practically immortal and no Sleeper can beat him. Despite hating him, she says he is the only thing holding the place together.

Sunny sees Nephis's cold, resolved look, the same she wore before the centurion and the demon, and knows this will become a problem. Effie tells her not to think about it and offers meat. Sunny eats ravenously, telling her he is from the outskirts. Nephis follows his example, but he knows she is unconvinced, since she is in the habit of making impossible things happen.

The desire to reach the castle has faded, though Sunny keeps a tiny hope that Effie is wrong. He does not really believe it, since she seems sincere and competent. Effie says there is not enough daylight to cross the ruins, so they will rest and leave at dawn. She dresses down the carcasses with a long knife, wearing a leather apron Memory, whistling like a gourmet chef.

Sunny feels as though someone pulled the batteries out of him. He compares it to running a marathon and finding another race beyond the finish line. He will never see Master Jet or Teacher Julius again, never become an Awakened, and never get rich. He tries to find solace: he is alive, they are safe from the sea, and there are hundreds of humans in the castle. Numbers and experience matter in the Dream Realm, and life there would be like a dream compared with the Labyrinth, if they are willing to submit to its master. There is also the outer settlement, and Effie seems to be doing fine on her own. He thinks maybe the situation seems terrible because it does not fit his inflated expectations, and decides Effie is happy because she expects nothing. His shadow does not seem convinced, and he does not feel better.

As night falls, the Crimson Spire's shadow crosses the city, filling him with dread. His shadow shows him the sea surging out of the crater, drowning the faceless woman statue until only her hand remains, and rising almost to the top of the granite wall, which holds it back like a dam. He walks over to Nephis and asks what she thinks. After a long silence, her eyes ignite with white sparks, and she says, 'We will find a way to return. No matter what has to be done, we will.'

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 130: Strength of a Dozen Men
chapters.chapter_summary:
In the morning Effie gives them instructions for crossing the city: follow behind her, listen to everything, make no noise, do not bleed, and do not think too much, because some creatures hear noisy thoughts and others sense strong emotions, so they must not feel fear. When Sunny asks how he is meant to control his feelings, she says to solve math equations in his head to impress a lovely lady, and teases him about getting too excited. She tells him to ask to be slapped if it is too much, and when he says it will not be a problem, she asks if he plays for the other team.

She rolls aside the granite slab blocking the tower exit, which weighs a couple of tons. Sunny asks how she is so strong, and she says it is her Aspect Ability, a strong all-around physical enhancement. She openly tells them her Flaw as well: it enhances her physical needs too, which is why she ate enough meat to leave a pile of bones. Sunny understands the price of having the hunger of many men in a place with little food, and he wonders if she became a huntress because she had no choice. When he starts wondering what other physical needs people have, she cackles and tells him not to get excited. He realizes she may be joking to lighten the mood and keep them calm, and tells her he is solving equations.

They leave the tower. Effie has summoned a Corinthian helmet with a tall blue horsehair crest and a narrow visor, and carries a leather bag on her back that is bigger inside than out. It is the fourth Memory Sunny has seen her summon, along with the apron and knife. He has yet to see what weapons she uses.

The ruins sprawl around the four of them like a vast, silent graveyard of stone. Sunny has to constantly remind himself that horrors hide in the shadows, and they must trust their guide. He has trouble imagining a situation where a writer would be useful, and then notices Effie's backside and pulls his thoughts out of the gutter. He is glad of the necessity to keep his emotions in check, because the danger of the ruins keeps them from dwelling on despair. They just have to take one step at a time.

Effie follows a convoluted path only she knows. They often stop and hide, sometimes cross open streets, crawl through rubble, pass through half-collapsed houses into secluded alleys, climb to rooftops, jump chasms, and cross rotten planks that someone placed over gaps. Nephis or Sunny carries Cassie in these places. Some interiors are so well preserved that they look as if the inhabitants left days ago. Everywhere there are signs of Effie's earlier visits and preparations, from planks across roofs to slabs hiding improvised passages. She has spent years turning parts of the maze into her private hunting ground, and makes crossing it look safe, though death is constantly breathing down their necks. They find freshly eviscerated carcasses and hear claws scraping stone and heavy footsteps, and each time she changes course or finds a perfect hiding place.

Sunny grows somber thinking he will have to learn everything she knows to feed himself, but takes comfort in having Nephis and Cassie, and is glad his Aspect gives him a version of her enhancement along with the ability to scout unseen. He does not offer her his shadow, in case something can sense its gaze. As the sun sinks, they reach the base of the hill with the castle, and Sunny's heart beats wildly, knowing their fate will change forever, for better or worse.

At the base of the hill stands a pristine white marble arch, untouched by the darkness. A wide road of white stones climbs the hill beyond it. Effie says that some areas of the ruins are avoided by many Nightmare Creatures, and the castle is one. When the original group of Sleepers arrived, only a single Spire Messenger nested in the throne room, and they killed it. Nephis asks what that is, and Effie says they are the big ugly pale creatures with black feathers they have seen hunting in the Labyrinth. They come from the Spire and are Fallen beasts, which is why she called the original group a little mad. The road winds up the hill, broken by stairs and elegant fortifications, with no guards. Effie says Gunlaug has barely enough people to man the walls, but they notice anything approaching, and have already spotted the four.

At the summit stands the castle, built of the same pristine marble, like a white mountain made by human hands. The front tower is wide, with a decorated gate and a grand staircase leading down to a vast platform, flanked by two bastion towers joined by arched bridges, with the main keep rising behind them as if challenging the Crimson Spire. The only blemish is dozens of human skulls hanging on rusty chains above the gates.

On the platform, hovels of rubble, rotting wood, and monster hides cling to the stones, and Sunny recognizes the stench of the slums. Gaunt, empty-eyed people in a mix of rags and shiny Memories, most barely older than Sunny, scratch out their existence. He nearly laughs at being back where he started, only worse off. Effie advises them to find an empty hut, or for two to pay the tribute and enter while the third stays. She points to her own cottage, says she does not host guests, and goes. Nephis takes out the two soul shards from the Rolling Stone, and they have to decide.

Nephis looks at the shards while the settlement's inhabitants hurry into their hovels as the Spire's shadow falls. She says they need to split up. When Sunny jokes about what happens when people split up, she says this is not a drama. They have enough shards to provide two of them with food and shelter for a week, and there is no reason to pass on that. Cassie asks about the third, and Sunny guesses who will stay outside. He thinks the bond they formed in the Labyrinth is already coming apart now that they are not the last three people in the world, and he has never lasted long in any group.

Nephis hands him the shards and tells him to take Cassie inside. He feels surprise, joy, concern, and also shame and resentment, and asks why him. She says she has never been noble or kind, and that it is the best choice: they need information, and with his shadow he can learn far more inside the castle, while she gathers information outside. They will meet in a week. She adds that their trade has ended, since his promise was to give up his share of spoils on the way to the castle, and the Rolling Stone was his kill. He realizes she assumes they will keep working together, and feels warm. Another string between them seems to snap, though.

He says he will meet her in a week, steps aside to let the girls say goodbye, and then leads Cassie up the grand stairs. Two armed guards in armor Memories scorn him and call him a rat. One takes the shards and tells him to go in. Looking up at the swinging skulls, Sunny leads Cassie through the gates, leaving Nephis alone in the night.

Past the gates is a large hall with tall stained-glass windows, where young women on creaking ladders drape thick sheets of crude fabric over them so that no light escapes at night. Behind them the gates close, and two guards slide an iron bolt into place. Sunny feels like an animal in a cage. A wooden desk in the hall looks like a hotel reception, and behind it sits a gaunt young man with nervous eyes, writing on parchment. He is Harper, responsible for guest accommodations today, and he welcomes them to the Bright Castle. He says he was once in their shoes, a few months ago, but Lord Gunlaug graced him with kindness, and Sunny cannot tell if he is sincere or just saying it for the guards.

Sunny notices that Harper is not surprised by when they arrived, and realizes the castle's people assume he and Cassie entered the Dream Realm near the ruins and spent two months scrounging for shards. He decides to keep it that way, since showing their true competence would attract unnecessary attention. Harper offers a room in the Tower of Dusk, which is quiet, and Sunny guesses it faces the Crimson Spire, which is why no one wants it. To Sunny, fewer people means less danger.

He gives their names as Sunless and Cassia. Harper writes them in a ledger with the date, and Sunny stares at the numbers: it has been seventy-seven days since they arrived on the Forgotten Shore, and back home spring is starting. Harper tells them they are completely safe between these walls, but throws a quick glance at the guards beside the sealed gate.

Harper leads them through the castle, explaining the rules. They may do what they want unless it breaks the rules of cohabitation. Some areas are open to everyone, and others are only for Gunlaug's host, marked by a serpent coiled around a tall tower. Sunny sees black tapestries with a white tower and a golden serpent, which he takes to represent the Dark City, the Bright Castle, and its lord. Harper adds that they must be respectful to the guards and hunters, who protect them and risk their lives, and if there is a misunderstanding they should be mindful of their burdens. Sunny translates this to 'don't mess with Gunlaug's people, and if they mess with you, swallow it.'

Inside, people seem surprisingly ordinary, with the usual worry and stress. Sunny thinks that humans adapt to anything, and that Gunlaug seems to provide stability, so maybe he is a necessary evil, as Effie said. They reach the westernmost tower, mostly empty because the Crimson Spire looms in the distance, though the windows are covered. It suits the two of them, since Cassie is blind and Sunny is used to the Spire.

Harper asks if they want one room or two, and Cassie and Sunny answer at the same time: 'One.' 'Two.' They freeze. Sunny asks for two adjacent rooms, or one if that is not possible. His habit of staying close to her has grown over months of camping together, and he does not trust anyone here. Harper gives him two iron keys, says food is served one hour after sunrise in the main hall of the Keep, and leaves. Cassie giggles and says she knows, he will scare everyone away like an overprotective, violent big brother. She says she does not feel safe either and that the place reminds her of a hotel. Sunny misses the police.

Sunny's room is tiny, with stone walls, a straw mattress, a flimsy chest, a desk with a basin, cloth strips, an oil lamp, and a small bronze mirror, and a narrow window with shutters draped in cloth. Letting light out of the castle at night is a severe crime, but neither he nor Cassie needs light. In the mirror he sees a stranger. His face is sharper, thin and pale, with dark circles and longer dirty black hair, and his eyes have a calm, heavy, bleak coldness. He realizes he has the look of a seasoned fighter, the 'murder math' that Hero and Nephis had, except that on him it looks like the eyes of a killer. Deeper down, only he can see golden threads of Weaver's legacy glowing in the dark. He grins and says, 'Looking good, Sunless.'

He leaves his shadow guarding Cassie's door and falls asleep on a real bed, surrounded by hundreds of people, marveling that days ago he was on a boat on the cursed sea. In the morning he waits in the hall. The Puppeteer's Shroud has finally had time to restore itself in the Soul Sea and looks clean. Cassie comes out glowing, in a light tunic and sandals, without her cloak, looking like a porcelain doll, and he thinks this smells like trouble. She says he smells different, and he jokes that she is saying he used to reek.

He guides her to the Keep, avoiding doors with the golden serpent symbol. Meals are served twice a day, in the morning and right before sunset. The castle's people look healthy, well-fed, young, and attractive, with more armor Memories than outside, though few compare to Cassie. When they enter the main hall of the Keep, hundreds of eyes turn to them.

The Keep's main hall is grand, with tall windows, white marble walls carved over dozens of meters, and at the far end, stairs leading to a dark alcove whose back wall is pierced with small holes, so light shines through like a fragment of starry night over an empty white throne. Long tables hold hundreds of Sleepers grouped in a hierarchy Sunny does not yet understand. He realizes they are staring at Cassie, not him. He scowls at them, gets two plates of monster-meat stew with vegetables and two cups of something like tea, and sits at a quiet end of a table. The stew has beetroot, Cassie says, and Sunny has never heard of it. Teacher Julius told him that if he ever saw something that looked familiar from Earth in the Dream Realm, he should turn and run.

He watches the hall through his shadow and expects trouble. Two rough young men rise and approach with vulgar smiles, wearing armor Memories and keeping swords visibly sheathed, apparently only to intimidate. Harper's advice about being respectful to Gunlaug's people echoes in Sunny's mind, but he responds aggressively. The hall goes silent and everyone watches him instead of Cassie.

The men call him an ugly clown and say they are Gunlaug's men. Sunny knows backing down would be a disaster, and tells them to get lost before he makes them dead men. One hesitates, then glances around at the watching crowd and cannot back down. They threaten to make him disappear, and Sunny prepares to summon the Midnight Shard. Then a calm voice behind him says, 'Leave them alone, please. They are my friends.' It is Caster.

It is Caster, the only person Sunny has seen defeat Nephis in a fight. At the Academy he was a star: handsome, friendly, humble, and respected even by other Legacies, some of whom thought he was the true king of the rankings and Nephis's first place a mistake. Sunny thinks he is his polar opposite. The two thugs stop wanting trouble, and one asks if he knows this guy. Caster says they were in the Academy together and that Sunny is rough around the edges but nice once you know him. Sunny is annoyed but understands that Caster is defusing the situation, since attacking Gunlaug's men on his first day would be a mess. The thugs warn Caster to teach him manners and go back to their seats.

Caster says it was not a very smart thing to do, and Sunny says who says he is smart. Caster sits down uninvited and says it is nice to see them both. Sunny asks if he is shocked to see them alive. Caster says it is good that they survived. At the Academy, he and Cassie were ranked last and shunned as walking corpses, and Sunny himself engineered that. Caster says they behaved like jerks and recalls fondly meeting Sunny, with the tall tales of spitting in awakened tyrants' faces and slaying sword saints with a shake of a finger.

Sunny, in the mood for mischief, claims that the most incredible thing he did in the Labyrinth was kill a Great Devil with one strike and get a Memory from it. He cannot show it because he ate it.

chapters.chapter_title: Chapter 139: The Incredible Adventures and Astonishing Deeds of Heroic Dreamer Sunless and His Beautiful Female Companions Princess Nephis and Lady Cassia, Abridged (Volume I)
chapters.chapter_summary:
Caster stares at him, then laughs. Cassie giggles at Sunny's earnest delivery. Caster says his sense of humor has not changed, and that few people manage to keep theirs here. Sunny insists it is the honest truth. As Caster laughs, Sunny thinks of Cassie's first dream of the Bright Castle: food, safety, and laughter, with Sunny leading her through its gates. Her visions are frighteningly accurate, and he wonders about her other vision.

He keeps going, listing his other adventures: slaying dozens of awakened creatures, being resurrected from death's door by a beautiful princess, summoning ancient horrors from the cursed sea, outsmarting ancient fiends, sailing through the abyss on a boat of demon bones, and fighting gargantuan leviathans underwater. Cassie stops laughing, struck by how outlandish it sounds in a list. Caster says his own story sounds lame, since he entered the Dream Realm near the wall, ran from monsters for a few days, and stumbled onto a hunting party from the castle. He asks when they arrived. Sunny cannot lie, and says two days ago, and that they entered the castle yesterday at dusk. Caster realizes they spent two months in the Labyrinth.

Sunny does not want to be seen as powerful, so he blames Nephis, saying they would have been dead without Changing Star, which he knows will make people think she carried them. Caster's face changes, and he asks intensely if Lady Nephis is alive and here. Sunny, irrationally angry, says she is around, and Cassie adds that they only had two shards, so she is in the outer settlement. Caster looks disappointed for a moment. He says only seven Sleepers were sent to the Shore this year, and he thought he was the only survivor. The other three are long dead, he says, and they quietly repeat 'May their souls rest in peace.'

After a silence, Sunny asks how Caster can afford the castle and whether he joined the golden serpent's army. Caster says no, though he has been tempted. All roads lead to Gunlaug, and few powerful Sleepers have stayed independent, and he is one of them. His Aspect Ability helps him escape Nightmare Creatures, but not kill them. He tried hunting with other independent hunters and barely escaped alive, but got a few shards, and sold a couple of Memories. Sunny notes that a Legacy enters with an arsenal of ancestral Memories, but only Masters and Saints can carry soul shards between realms, so even rich clans cannot feed their scions too much in advance. Caster's Memories could buy him months or years of comfort in the castle, an enormous advantage even here.

Sunny asks why Gunlaug's men were afraid of him. Caster explains that those two were Castle Guards, at the bottom of the totem pole, weak and inexperienced, and his minor reputation makes them think twice. For a second there is a dangerous gleam in his eyes, and Sunny remembers that Legacies are trained to fight and kill from childhood. He hopes never to face him in battle. Caster warns that the Host itself will not react to the guards' humiliation, but if they had been Hunters or Pathfinders, even his name would not have protected Sunny, and that the castle can be as dangerous as the city, especially for someone with Sunny's temperament.

Cassie asks if there is really no way out. Caster, after a long silence, says there is none that any of them can ever hope to reach, but perhaps something will change. He says his quarters are in the Tower of Dawn and leaves, and Sunny's stew is cold. Later, lying on his bed in the quiet Tower of Dusk, Sunny decides it is time to send his shadow for a walk.

Over the next five days Sunny mostly stays in his room while his shadow prowls the castle, spying and learning secrets. The seemingly peaceful castle is built on a fragile balance, with a system that lets the abused dream of a better life and restrains the abusers from going too far. Better life means winning Gunlaug's favor, while going too far means banishment to the outer settlement. Both fear and hope are held firmly by the Bright Lord. The castle and slum form a closed cycle, like a serpent biting its tail, that paradoxically keeps everyone sane and alive. Sunny wants no part of it.

About five hundred Sleepers live in the castle, in a complex hierarchy. Most serve Gunlaug directly as Guards, Hunters, Pathfinders, Artisans, and Handmaidens, led by five lieutenants who answer directly to him. The Castle Guard is the largest, about a hundred and fifty men who guard the stronghold and enforce the laws. They are near the bottom, recruited from anyone with a vaguely useful Aspect Ability, and see little combat apart from stray monsters. Their leader is Tessai, a morose giant, one of Gunlaug's most trusted lieutenants and perhaps the oldest Sleeper on the Shore at just two years short of thirty.

Above them are about fifty Hunters, the elite, in seven hunting parties, one of which leaves each morning to hunt awakened creatures so everyone can eat. Hunters are recruited from the Guard and get their own rooms, better food, luxuries, and the best Memories, but often die young. Fewer than a dozen Pathfinders, seasoned veterans who know large areas of the city, guide them. Both are led by a charismatic man called Gemma, who came to the Shore the same year as Gunlaug and helped him take the castle. Together, Guards, Hunters, and Pathfinders form the Host.

Two other groups belong to Gunlaug. The Artisans, about a hundred people, mostly assistants, are Sleepers with Utility Abilities and their helpers who make clothes, tools, equipment, and gear. They are led by a young woman called Kido, a talented manager whose Ability changes the attributes of certain plants, and the vegetables in Sunny's stew come from her garden. Such an Ability is priceless on the Shore, which is why she became a lieutenant despite being younger than the rest. The Artisans' status is tense: the Guards feel non-combatants should rank lower, and the Artisans think their rarity and importance deserve more prestige. Hunters do not care, and Gemma quietly supports Kido, which keeps the Guards from pressing too hard.

The Handmaidens, also about a hundred, are the young women who do chores like closing windows and serving food, and who maintain the castle and serve high-ranking members. Sunny expected them to be the main victims of abuse, but they are strangely revered and a little feared because of their leader, a mysterious, strikingly beautiful woman named Seishan, who secretly teaches them to defend themselves. They also technically belong to Gunlaug, who is particular about people touching his belongings. The first time Sunny's shadow watched them, Seishan suddenly turned and looked directly at where it hid, the first time anyone sensed it. He shut his eyes and pulled his perception back, and has avoided her ever since.

The last hundred are tenants who pay tribute but do not serve directly, some providing entertainment or services, like a music lounge, a theatre troupe, and a gambling den, and others like Harper doing menial jobs. At the top is the golden serpent, the Bright Lord Gunlaug. On his fifth day in the castle, Sunny finally lays eyes on him, and does not like what he sees.

Gunlaug's presence permeates the castle, but he rarely shows himself and rules through his five proxies. Sunny avoids him, afraid after the Seishan incident. On the fifth day, as he and Cassie are about to receive breakfast, the hall goes silent and Guards pour in and push the tables against the walls. Sunny fears the worst, but they ignore him. He sees Caster in the crowd, solemn, looking toward the alcove.

Five figures step out of the dark and stand at the foot of the throne: Gemma, Tessai, Seishan, Kido, and the fifth lieutenant, who makes Sunny shudder. Everyone fears him most, though he has no official duties. He is a pale, bony-faced man with glassy, emotionless eyes and a twisted spine that makes him look short, dressed in plain black. His name is Harus, Gunlaug's hidden blade and executioner. If Gunlaug wants his displeasure known there are rivers of blood, and if not people simply disappear. Many have had nightmares of his eyes staring from the dark. Looking at Harus is like looking at a dark mirror, and Sunny sees traces of a possible future version of himself.

Then the tall man steps from the darkness in a gilded armor that covers him from head to toe, including the eyes, looking both solid and liquid. Where his face should be is a smooth polished gold expanse reflecting hundreds of frightened faces. Sunny's legs tremble and everyone around him is pale and sweating, even the lieutenants. Protected by the Shroud's [Doubtless], Sunny realizes it is a mind attack triggered by looking at the mirror-like face, and Cassie, being blind, is unaffected. Gunlaug sits on the white throne, and a deep voice seems to come from the castle itself: 'A perfect day for justice… I've heard there's a criminal hiding among us today.'

Sunny wants to fall to his knees and beg forgiveness, and knows everyone feels the same, since everyone has done something Gunlaug might call a crime. Two guards drag a man in rags into the center of the hall and throw him down. He is painfully lean, a dweller of the outer settlement, with ropes of muscle under thin skin and a proud, furious look. He stands with his head held high, grimaces at his reflection in the golden face, but does not lower his gaze. Sunny is impressed by his willpower.

Gunlaug announces that the man, Jubei, has been accusing one of his men and has been invited to plead his case. Despite not feeling the armor's pressure, Sunny still gets goosebumps from the Bright Lord's soft, ingratiating voice. Jubei points at a group of Hunters and accuses an older Pathfinder of murder. He says the Pathfinder and his party lured a naive kid into their group with promises of rewards and a life in the castle, then fed him to monsters as bait. He says he saw it himself while hunting that day.

People in the hall go grim. They are used to ignoring wicked deeds by humans against humans, but a human betraying another to Nightmare Creatures is sacrilege. Gunlaug asks the Pathfinder, who calmly says the boy was a highly valued member of his party and his death saddened everyone. Gunlaug sighs that it is Jubei's word against his and implies that distrusting his men would be wicked. Then Gemma suggests the right of challenge: if Jubei doubts his accusation he should step down, or he can challenge the criminal and prove it with blood, and as the person responsible for the Hunters, the real culprit is Gemma himself. Jubei, furious, says 'I challenge you!'

Sunny knows the performance is orchestrated and that it is an execution. He cannot tell whether Gemma and the Pathfinder rehearsed it or improvised for their lord, who wants everyone to see what happens to those who speak against him. Still, a small ember of hope remains that Jubei, a strong, seasoned hunter, might win. Gunlaug accepts the challenge as a sacred tradition, but says Gemma cannot represent the accused because the castle cannot afford to lose him, and asks if Jubei would mind if the accused chose another champion. Jubei shrugs, 'Bring your worst.' The Pathfinder, pale, says in a quiet voice, 'I choose Harus, my lord.'

The hall goes silent. Jubei smirks, 'Even better,' as if he has a score to settle with the hunchback. Harus walks down the steps, looking a little bored. Gemma frowns, Tessai grins, Kido pales and steps away, and Seishan remains cold and unreadable. Cassie asks Sunny to leave, but he says they cannot, since leaving would draw attention, and he must gather information. He also feels that someday, he and Harus will end up bloody with only one walking away, as if connected by a thread of fate.

Jubei summons a flexible armor of red scales, a winged helmet, a kite shield, and a curved scimitar. Harus drops his cloak, straightens his spine until he towers above nearly everyone except Tessai, and summons nothing. Jubei lunges, fast and nimble, but Harus catches the blade with his bare fist, and no one can wrench it free. He puts a hand on Jubei's shoulder and tears off the whole arm. Before the pain arrives he grips his head and snaps his neck, then punches his chest and sends the body flying a dozen meters. It takes five seconds. Harus shakes the blood off his hands and returns to Gunlaug's side, glee on his face. This is justice.

The Sleepers stare at the body of Jubei, whose scale armor dissolves into light, leaving him in torn, bloody rags with a dazed expression. It is a reminder never to disobey Gunlaug. Sunny is one of the only two people not looking at the corpse, and instead watches Harus, who stares at the wall, uninterested. He understands how hopeless it is to challenge the Golden Serpent. Since all humans in the Dark City have the same dormant core, power comes only from Soul Essence and Memories, and both are monopolized by Gunlaug, who alone has the manpower and knowledge to hunt freely. Any crumbs that independent hunters get end up with him through the tribute system. Shards and Memories make the Host stronger, which brings in more of both, a cycle that grows more absolute with each turn.

Sunny suspects most of the Host's elite have their cores saturated with Soul Essence, and with no way to advance to the next rank, the group inside these walls may be the most powerful group of Sleepers in human history. And Nephis wants to kill their leader. He remembers Effie's words and the skulls over the gate. He decides he must persuade her to give up, but doubts she knows how.

Gunlaug leaves, the lieutenants follow, Harus last, the body is dragged away, and Handmaidens wipe the blood. People return to breakfast as if nothing happened, and Sunny has lost his appetite. For the remaining two days he gathers information boldly, spying on Hunters and Pathfinders, Guard training, and the engravings on the walls, avoiding only the Handmaidens. On the eighth day, he and Cassie come to the gates. Harper asks if they will pay tribute for another week, and Sunny pretends to be sad that they cannot afford it. They leave, and Cassie asks what to do next. He says they will go find Nephis.

Cassie asks how they will find Nephis, and Sunny says they will follow the sounds of mayhem, since few people in the outer settlement have armor Memories. They descend into the slum, where some people look at them with pity as the newly exiled and others gloat. The contrast with the castle strikes him: people in the castle have mundane human worries, but here people merely exist, gaunt, cold, listless, driven by the need to find food and the fear of being eaten at night. Hope only appears when they glance at the Bright Castle. He thinks it is not so different from the outskirts, with the added terror of Nightmare Creatures, though in the real world the monsters wore human skin.

He sees no sign of Nephis until they reach the edge of the slum, where an unusually spacious dwelling stands above a vertical drop, crudely built from slabs scavenged from the ruins, some still carved with the original inhabitants' designs. It is closest to the white stone road and has a small addition on top like a second storey. Nephis sits on its roof in a crude tunic with a rope belt, her armor dismissed, watching the sunrise. She jumps down, and Sunny says, 'Hey, Neph. Long time no see!'

Inside, the lodge is spartan and drafty, with broken furniture. It was empty because no one wants to live this close to the road, where monsters attack. Cassie gives Nephis the supper she saved. Nephis uncovers a pile of juicy roasted meat on the table, enough for ten people in the castle for a day or two. A big monster came from the road a few nights ago, she says, and she and a few others killed it, and this is her share. The Castle Guard fights monsters that attack the castle from the slopes or sky, but not those coming along the road. When Sunny asks why she chose this pit, she says it is quiet here, and she likes it.

From the window there is a vista of the ruined city, and Nephis says what can compete with such a killer view. A ghastly wail answers from far away. They eat on the floor, passing Cassie's glass bottle around, almost like old times. Nephis asks what Sunny learned in the castle, and he describes the order of things, the six castes, and how they relate, with Cassie adding details.

Nephis questions the numbers. If about five hundred live in the castle and almost as many in the settlement, the population of the Dark City is around a thousand, mostly young, which means hundreds arrive each year and most survive. Yet she has not seen a Sleeper of their year in the slum, and thinks the three of them are the only ones. Sunny reluctantly adds that Caster is also there, living comfortably, and Nephis grows strangely animated. Sunny explains that Caster said only seven Sleepers were sent to the Shore this year. There seems to be a pattern: fifteen years ago a dozen a year, then a few dozen, then a hundred, then several hundred, and this year seven. Since the Spell loves the number seven, some think it marks the end of a fourteen-year cycle. Caster learned the number through an Artisan whose revelation Ability traces the general location of everyone a person has met, and she found six.

He covers the rest, including Jubei's trial. Cassie grows pale and Nephis's face darker. He concludes that Gunlaug controls food, shelter, hope, fear, and even power itself, and may as well be a god. Nephis says he is just an impostor. She asks why no one has killed him in his sleep or why a lieutenant did not stage a coup. Sunny says that was only Gunlaug's power as a ruler, and his personal power is much worse.

Sunny says Effie was right that Gunlaug may as well be immortal. Besides having absorbed more Soul Essence than anyone and more experience, there is more. Nephis asks if his Aspect Ability is uniquely powerful, and Sunny says it lets him breathe and move with incredible speed underwater. Gunlaug came to the city about eight years ago, and the ability was useless in the ruins, so he became an outcast, in a bloody, brutal time when strength decided everything. But he was mad even by those standards, and began hunting in the dark sea. At dusk he dove from the wall to scavenge soul shards from monsters of the Labyrinth crushed by the flood, racing the horrors of the depths, and at dawn he dove into the retreating sea to scavenge meat from what they left. Nephis, who has met the things in the sea twice, is silent.

One day a current carried him away, and when the sea receded he found a mortally wounded leviathan, and began cutting meat from its bones. It died at that exact moment, and since his blade was the last to cut it, the Spell credited him with the kill, which gave him a Memory: a golden armor that no human weapon can scratch. Sunny and Nephis once saw two centurions take Transcendent soul shards from a leviathan carcass, so the armor is at least three ranks above every human core on the Shore, and it has no openings. With it he returned, gathered supporters, killed everyone who stood in his way, and took the castle.

Nephis asks about its traits. Sunny says it is liquid metal and emits crushing psychic pressure, but only when one looks at their reflection in the visor, so Cassie was unaffected. He tries to convince Nephis to give up any idea of going against Gunlaug. She says she learned something too: there is a Gateway here after all, in the Crimson Spire.

The Crimson Spire is the eerie shadow that has hunted Sunny all along, standing at the center of the Labyrinth like an axis between heaven and earth, and the background for the last part of Cassie's vision. Instructor Rock said that without a human Citadel the Gateway would be inside or around the region's most prominent landmark. Sunny remembers that Rock also said to defeat the Gateway guardians together, and asks what guards the Spire. Nephis says a Fallen Terror, the class above tyrants with six soul cores. Going there is suicide, since the chance of beating one is zero, even less than breaking through Gunlaug's armor. Sunny finds it a cruel irony to be trapped and stare at the way out every day, which explains why the Tower of Dusk is unpopular.

Nephis says the first ruler of the castle led an expedition to find a way out of the Labyrinth and all died, and the second, the last of the original cohort, tried to reach the Gateway and also died. After that, no one tried. Everything Effie said is true: they will spend the rest of their lives here. When Sunny asks about the plan, Nephis says they will create a hunting party, and that they need a pathfinder. She has someone in mind, and they will go see her later. First she wants every detail Sunny learned in the castle: names, Aspects, Abilities, Flaws, grievances, and hidden agendas.

Several hours later, Sunny finishes his report, including that the Pathfinder Jubei accused is a gambler who spends all his shards in Aiko's gambling den, refuses to pay, and hurts those who object. Some say the challenge happened because he wanted to hunt a powerful monster to pay part of his debt. Cassie praises him. Sunny asks who the pathfinder is, and Nephis says everyone worth something has a party except one person, and that it will not be easy: it is Effie.

They stand before a stone cabin better built than most of the settlement's hovels, with a large bestial skull split by a sharp weapon hung above the door. Nephis knocks, then bangs, until a sleepy voice says whoever it is had better be a Nightmare Creature. Before the door opens, Nephis tells Sunny and his shadow to turn away. When Effie opens it, Nephis flatly asks her to put on a Memory. A light fades from a provocatively short chiton, and Effie, wearing nothing underneath, asks if that is better. She is as tall and strong as before. She asks if the other two look so clean and shiny because the castle was pleasant, and Sunny answers that the ambiance is an acquired taste.

Inside, Effie's cabin has a bed of furs, each from a Nightmare Creature, a fireplace, a table with one chair, two chests, and curios from the ruins. She wraps in a fur and asks what they want so early, though it is noon. Nephis asks if she has hunted since they met, and Effie says not yet, and will go back when her food runs out in a day or two, even though she butchered enough meat to feed someone for months. Nephis says to come with them and be their pathfinder.

Effie laughs, saying she refused all the best hunters. Nephis guesses it is because her Flaw means she cannot share spoils. Effie says that is not it: the hunters are weak, because Gunlaug will never allow anyone strong to exist outside his control. Sunny points out that he is allowing her to exist, and she only raises an eyebrow. Nephis says they are not weak, having killed dozens of awakened creatures. Effie says that was there and this is the Dark City, and that if they survive a few years they can talk again. Nephis smiles darkly: 'We will talk again in the evening. Then, you will change your mind.'

With the sun past its zenith, Sunny cannot imagine what Nephis can do before evening, but her face is determined and white flames dance in her eyes. She walks toward the castle, telling them to follow. She asks about the Pathfinder accused of murder three days ago, and Sunny repeats what he knows. His Aspect Ability makes any weapon in his hands incredibly sharp, enough to cut stone, maybe steel. She asks about his Flaw, and Sunny says people protect their Flaws, not like that lunatic Effie. Cassie, who is protective of him today, adds that they do not even know Sunny's Flaw, and he almost stumbles, since he never shared his.

At the gates, Nephis tells them they do not need to do anything but follow her and try to look virtuous. Two Guards block their way with contemptuous, suggestive looks, asking if they want to pay tribute or get paid. Nephis says she wants to enter but will not pay tribute. When the guards demand to know why she is wasting their time, she says she is here to invoke the Right of Challenge.

Sunny's heart pounds. He thinks she has gone mad, then remembers she is always cool-headed, so she must see something he does not. The guards warn her that it is a fight to the death and no one will go easy because of her face. She nods. One Guard leads them in, remarking it is a shame, since with her looks she could live in the castle without paying tribute. Harper is still at his desk and asks, confused, why Sunless and Cassia are back. Sunny wants to palm his face, since 'maybe we will see each other again' did not mean the same day. Harper asks if they got shards, and Sunny says not exactly.

News of the challenge has not yet spread, so only a few dozen people have gathered in the grand hall, though their number is growing. Sunny whispers asking if she is really going to fight one of Gunlaug's lieutenants, which would be suicide. Nephis says only 'The walls have ears.' The Guard tells them to come in. Inside, whispers rise about who she is. Most lieutenants are not there, and neither is Gunlaug. Only Gemma, the leader of Hunters and Pathfinders, sits on the steps below the empty throne, looking sullen, and to Sunny's relief Harus is absent.

Gemma asks if one of them wants to invoke the Right of Challenge. Nephis says she does, calmly. He tries to dissuade her, saying throwing her life away is stupid and she should reconsider, and he sounds sincere. She says no need. He asks who she is here to accuse, and she names the Pathfinder Andel. Gemma reminds her that any crime committed on duty is his, and asks if she is sure she wants to challenge him. Nephis says she is not here about the murder of the boy but about theft: Andel lost a considerable amount of shards gambling and refused to pay, which is stealing, and since it happened on his private time, Gemma has nothing to do with it. Sunny finds it ingenious, because the lieutenants cannot fight on his behalf without breaking their claim of justice.

Gemma is baffled and asks if Aiko sent her. Nephis says she has never met her, and that she does not need to know the victim to punish the criminal. When he offers to pay the shards himself, she says it is not about shards but about justice and law, repeating that the law is their guiding star, which Gunlaug said days earlier. Gemma has little choice, and orders Andel brought. He asks her name so she will at least be remembered. Nephis says in a clear voice: 'I am Changing Star of the Immortal Flame clan.' Everything goes silent.

Everyone is quiet, even Gemma. Only Caster, who entered the hall earlier and stands by a wall with a complex expression, does not react. Her full name is shocking for two reasons. She used a True Name, which almost no Awakened in history has earned in the First Nightmare, and none of the thousand Sleepers on the Shore, not even Gunlaug, has one. And she announced herself a Legacy of the Immortal Flame clan, which helped humanity conquer the Second and Third Nightmares. She could be seen as almost messianic here. A tentative glow of hope appears in some eyes. She chooses that moment to summon her armor, and the Starlight Legion Armor appears with seven stars on its breastplate. The crowd recognizes the Starlight Crest, the crest of the Seven, carved on the giant statue's robe and on the castle's walls, representing the seven heroes who vowed to vanquish the darkness. Sunny sweats, worried that if people think she is a savior, Gunlaug will come knocking.

Gemma recovers, and smiles, saying it is an impressive name and that one wonders where it came from, insinuating she is lying. Many lose their wistful expressions, though some still look at her with timid faith. Nephis remains calm.

Andel enters: average height, solid build, shaved sides and a short braid, around twenty-four, a ruthless veteran. He says he was sad to let Harus have all the fun last time. Gemma says he will show him real fun after he kills the girl. Andel's falchion becomes razor sharp, sharp enough that even the Starlight Legion Armor would not stop it. Nephis does not draw. He lunges with inhuman speed, and she sidesteps and throws her arms up, summoning her longsword, whose sparks pass through the falchion and take shape behind it, and the blade cleanly severs his head. Silence falls. She picks up the head by the hair, looks up at Gemma, and says with a polite smile, 'Oh. It was nice to meet you too.'

Nephis leaves the castle holding Andel's dripping head by the hair, with the indifferent expression of someone who has done it before, and Sunny wonders how many people she has killed. People in the castle look at her as an avenging angel or a demon. The settlement's reaction is quiet but more intense, a dark, sweltering emotion. Sunny is uneasy, since if she does not know the storm she created things could go bad fast, and it is worse if she does it deliberately.

They reach Effie's cabin at sunset, as Nephis promised. Effie opens the door before they knock, irritated, and Nephis throws the head at her feet and asks if they can talk now. Effie goes grim and says to come inside, then furiously whispers what the hell Nephis has done. Nephis says she wanted her to prove her strength. Sunny says that Nephis just killed Andel with one strike in front of everyone, and she is Changing Star of the Immortal Flame clan, the champion of justice. Effie bursts into laughter, delighted, and says she wishes she had seen their faces. Then she warns them that when she refused to join the Host, Gunlaug made it clear that if he cannot have her, no one will, and any group that invited her has regretted it, so hiring her puts them in his crosshairs. Sunny says it is a bit late to worry.

Next morning, a crowd of slum dwellers sees them off, curious about the Starlight Legion Armor's symbol. The story has already grown. Sunny asked Nephis how she beat a stronger opponent so easily, and she said it was an old Legacy trick. As they set off, the crowd parts for Caster, who bows and says he, Caster of the Han Li clan, would like to join their hunting party. Nephis shrugs, 'If you want.' He addresses the group as Lady Nephis, Huntress Athena, Cassia, and Sunny. He becomes the fifth member, and the five step onto the white road into the ruins.

Their first hunt is surprisingly uneventful. With Effie guiding and Sunny's shadow scouting, they avoid Fallen creatures and reach the target, where they hide and wait. Effie describes the monster's strengths and weaknesses and Nephis assigns roles. Nephis will take the risk and lure the enemy into exposing a vulnerability, but Caster, not Sunny, will deliver the killing blow, since his Ability is a powerful combat one and Sunny's is not officially. Sunny feels replaced, but swallows his bitterness. The monster dies without injuries, and Nephis and Caster work together harmoniously, probably because both were trained as Legacies. Sunny and Effie, who stayed with Cassie, do nothing. Effie laughs that it was the easiest meal she has ever earned. She is not an official member, but a hired worker who guides and informs.

They butcher the creature and carry the meat back. At the marble arch, Nephis gives Effie her share and asks the other three to entrust their parts of the meat to her. Cassie agrees, Caster bows and agrees, and Sunny, not having done anything but lend his shadow, grudgingly agrees. At the settlement, she splits the meat, a small portion for Cassie to feed them until the next hunt, and a much larger pile that she puts in front of the lodge. When someone asks her price, since hunters usually sell part of their spoils, she says the party will not sell meat, ever. They will give it away for free.

The crowd distrusts her, and someone shouts that it is a trick. She replies that there is no trick, and asks if she is not human, and are they not, and whether a human needs a reason to help others of her kind. She tells them shame on them for forgetting who they are, since they are people, not beasts, and tells them to take food. They come one by one, taking a strip and hurrying off, with a timid new light on their faces, faith or hope. Sunny watches Guards on the castle walls, and thinks Nephis is right that they are people, but people are much worse than beasts.

After that day, everything moves so fast that Sunny feels pulled along by a current, afraid of being left behind. Nephis leads several more hunts and always gives most of the spoils away free, so the party must hunt every other day. Sunny spends most of his time with Effie, serving as her scout and learning the city, so the party rarely meets anything it cannot handle. Their flawless record makes them known as the strongest hunters in the slum, and some think they equal the castle's Hunters. Nephis is known since the duel with Andel, Effie was already respected, and Caster is quickly adored for his charm and skill. Cassie is loved because Nephis has her hand out the free meat. Sunny is overlooked, treated as a support member or charity case, and he is both glad and furious that no one knows how powerful he is. Nephis spends most of her time with Caster, and when Sunny's frustration builds, he trains his katas with the Midnight Shard until his muscles hurt.

Other changes worry him more. People distrust Nephis, then thank her, then revere her, and some jokingly call her Saint Nephis, with less humor each day. Sunny fears that kings never go easy on meddling messiahs. Random young people from the settlement start to help around the lodge with hides, tools, and food, and some ask Sunny if he is new, which they never do to Caster.

One night Cassie wakes him, whispering that something is coming from the road. He, Nephis, and Caster fight a devil that wandered up the hill, and drive it off before it reaches the settlement. At dawn people see the claw marks and blood and Nephis leaning on her sword. Sunny realizes that she has given them food, safety, hope, and the fear of the castle's people after Andel, and only power remains, and that it was all deliberate. He still does not know her ultimate goal.

About a month into living in the settlement, Sunny wakes with the familiar feeling of not belonging anywhere. Outside he finds a gaunt, ragged young man near the lodge door, whom he recognizes as Harper, the receptionist from the castle. Harper admits he could not pay the tribute and was expelled, and asks if he can get food. Sunny tells him to talk to a red-haired girl in charge of breakfast and says they give meat after hunts and let guests help out. Harper brightens at the thought of free food.

Inside, Nephis and Caster are discussing a big joint hunt with several hunters from other parties, apparently starting without him. The lodge has been transformed, with furniture, hides, and a large map of the Dark City on the wall. A hunter proposes the area south of a collapsed lighthouse, where creatures have sharp hearing, and Caster suggests deceiving their hearing. Sunny offers his Memory bell, but his voice drowns out, and when he tries again, everyone turns their backs. He walks away feeling invisible and sits on the roof, sending his shadow around the lodge.

Harper seems off. He is helping with dishes and asking newcomers' questions, and an hour later slips away through the slum into a dark alley, where a high-ranking Guard waits. Harper says he has done what he was told, and the Guard says he can return to the castle without tribute if he learns everything about the cohort's core members, including Saint Nephis's Aspect, Abilities, and Flaws. Harper says he knows a couple of them already, including Lady Changing Star's scout, a friend. The Guard says rats like Sunny will talk if shown a little respect. Harper hesitates, asks if they will be hurt, and gets a mocking answer, and does not object. Sunny plans to beat Harper and throw him out, but Effie shouts that the hunt is starting.

The joint party of almost twenty leaves at noon, heading east toward a collapsed lighthouse at the city's edge, with Effie as chief pathfinder and Sunny scouting ahead. The plan is simple, but nothing in the Dark City is safe. Halfway there, Effie freezes, listens, and shouts 'Scatter!' as the hunters dash apart. Sunny grabs Cassie and dives aside as something huge crashes onto the cobblestones where they stood. Two hunters are too slow, and their screams drown in tearing flesh. His shadow is not near, so Sunny must fight without it, and he summons the Midnight Shard. A massive winged creature with a pale body and black feathers, a Spire Messenger, stands in the street, its beak open with needle-like fangs, licking blood off its face.

Sunny is paralyzed for a moment, then covers Cassie. The hunters decide to attack together, since a familiar enemy is better than the unknown, hoping to drive the Fallen beast away. Their Memories cannot pierce its hide, but strikes still hurt. It spears one hunter through armor and nearly tears another apart before Caster pulls him away with his speed. Effie summons a weapon and leaps forward, her whole body like a spring, and the tip breaks the pale hide of its chest and stabs deep. The creature lashes out and she raises a round shield and takes the blow, cracking the stones, but she remains standing, spits blood, grins, and twists the weapon. The Messenger screams, sweeps the hunters back with its wings, picks up the dead hunters, and flies off.

Effie says her arm may be broken, and laughs. Sunny wants to congratulate her, but then sees her weapon for the first time: an ancient, beautiful bronze spear. Something clicks in his mind, and he finally understands the future.

Effie asks if he is okay, and Sunny says he is just thinking. Alone, he lowers himself to the ground with a phrase repeating in his head: a woman with a bronze spear drowning in a tide of monsters. It is part of Cassie's vision from the night on the headless knight statue. He recalls the vision: the castle at night, burning under a lonely star, rivers of blood in its halls, a corpse in golden armor on a throne, a woman with a bronze spear drowning in a tide of monsters, and an archer trying to pierce the falling sky.
