He had assumed all of it was about the past. Effie's spear shows him that the images were not the past but the future.

He glances at Nephis, who is healing wounded hunters with a painful grimace, and sees that she is the lonely star that burns above the Bright Castle, bringing fire and blood, since her name can be read as Star of Ruin. He had been afraid of what Gunlaug would do to her, and should have feared what she would do to him. The corpse in golden armor on a throne is Gunlaug, the woman is Effie, and the archer is someone he has yet to meet. Nephis has an overwhelming goal and must return to the real world. Her words, 'No matter what has to be done, we will,' take on a darker meaning. The only way out is the Gateway in the Spire, and it would need an army. To get one, she would have to kill Gunlaug, take his power, eliminate opposition, and rally every Sleeper into a suicidal crusade. Most would die, and no sane person would follow her, but he remembers the reverence in her followers' eyes.

On the way back he feels like he is in a fever dream. He tells himself that as long as he is the one left standing, he might benefit, and Gunlaug dying solves one problem, but he is terrified anyway. At sunset he goes to the edge of the platform, thinks that all these people will die, and wonders whether he is willing to help her. A gaunt figure approaches. He had forgotten Harper, who says, 'Sunless! Uh… can we talk?'

Harper stands with a pathetic, timid smile, and Sunny feels an urge to erase it. His mind is half drowned in the terror of the vision, but he decides not to expose the spy, since the best way to deal with a mole is to feign ignorance and feed him false information. He is a master of deception, though he cannot lie, and Harper picked the perfect mark. Harper thanks him for inviting him into the lodge and offers to share a rare bottle of liquor from the Artisans' garden at his hut. Sunny agrees, seeing it as a chance to find out what Harper's plan is and feed him truths along with lies, then report to Nephis in the morning.

Harper's hut is a pathetic shelter of rotting wood with a seaweed thatch mattress and a low table. He pours a milky liquor into a chipped clay cup, and Sunny, who avoided alcohol all his life, downs it and feels warmth and sweet solace. Harper asks about the Spire Messenger and whether Sunny was with Changing Star for two months in the Labyrinth, and Sunny, flushed, plays the jealous freeloader, claiming he saved her life many times, then blurts out, 'and for what?' and that this was not supposed to happen. Harper takes it as the liquor working and asks if he has seen Nephis's Ability. Sunny says it can be used to heal, which makes Harper conclude she is only a healer, and Sunny hopes other spies will report the same.

Then Harper asks how Nephis got her True Name, and Sunny, careless from terror and drink, says 'Probably the same way I did.' He freezes, laughs it off, and Harper laughs too, then jokingly asks what his True Name is. The pressure of the Flaw builds in Sunny's mind. Harper sees something is wrong. Before the pain forces the answer out, Sunny picks up the crude iron knife and stabs it through Harper's heart.

Sunny drives the knife in, flinging the table against the wall, and presses his hand over Harper's face so no sound escapes. Harper's eyes ask why. Feeling hot blood, Sunny lets the Flaw's pain overwhelm him and whispers his True Name into the dying man's ear, 'Lost from Light,' as Harper weakly smears blood and tears on his face. Biting his lips until they bleed, Sunny twists the knife until the eyes grow still. The Spell announces that he has slain Dreamer Harper and that his shadow grows stronger.

Sunny vomits and crawls away, telling himself that Harper was going to sell them out to Gunlaug, but cannot accept it. He admits aloud that he killed him because he wanted to survive and because it was easy, and feels better, since he is already a murderer and plans to help Nephis kill hundreds. He vomits again, thinking about the body and the noise of the broken table.

When he sits up, the door is open, and Caster stands there, pale, taking in the broken table, the smell of alcohol, the corpse with a knife in its chest, and Sunny covered in blood. Sunny says he killed the bastard, in a calm voice, because he cannot show weakness to Caster, whom he does not trust. He says Harper asked too many questions about Nephis's Ability and True Name, and that Tessai sent him as a spy, which he saw that morning. Caster asks for proof, and Sunny wonders whether he will have to kill him too. Caster says he believes him, since he suspected Harper too, but others might not, as Sunny has a bad-temper reputation, and with alcohol and no proof that Harper worked for the castle, it looks bad. He offers to help conceal everything, but no one can ever know, especially Lady Nephis. It will be their secret, and he smiles.

Sunny knows what Caster is doing. He grew up in the outskirts, and when Caster says he will help, what he means is that he will own him, because there is no better leverage than a gruesome secret. But unless Sunny is ready to kill him on the spot, he cannot refuse, and what Caster thinks will happen and what will really happen are not set in stone. He forces a smile and thanks him. Caster tells him to wait while he brings something to clean himself, and they will then need to get rid of the body, which will not be easy to do unnoticed. Sunny sends his shadow to watch Caster, and sits by the wall next to Harper's open, accusing eyes, knowing a new shadow has joined the ranks in his Soul Sea.

Caster takes a long time, since he has to avoid prying eyes and talk to people who want his attention, and Sunny hears Cassie ask Caster if he has seen Sunny. In the dark, listening to rain on the stones, which always puts him in a bad mood, Sunny remembers his past. His parents were menial workers: his father worked on a crew maintaining the city's outer barriers, and his mother in an underground factory making air filtration systems. They barely afforded a small cell in a hive in the outskirts. When Sunny was around four, several months after his sister Rain was born, his father died in a work accident. Three years later his mother got sick and died. The two were sent to a government child care facility, where Rain, young and cute, was adopted, but Sunny, older and with 'behavioral problems,' was not. After a few years in increasingly vile foster homes, he ran away and learned to survive on the streets. He survived because of luck and intelligence, but mostly because he refused to die before finding his sister, believing she was waiting for him to save her.

He chuckles that it did not end well, and wonders if there is such a thing as a happy ending. His shadow shows Caster raising his hand to open the hut's door, and Sunny tiredly shakes off his memories, telling himself he has to survive the future.

Caster brings water, cloth strips, and a plain tunic. While Sunny washes, Caster moves Harper's body to a corner under the seaweed thatch and wipes up the blood, though close scrutiny would still reveal it. He explains that the easiest way to dispose of a corpse is to throw it off the platform, but since Harper worked for the Bright Lord, the Guards will take an interest, and they have to make him disappear completely. Castle Guard observers watch the road day and night, and Caster says he can pay them to look away. Tomorrow after sunset, Sunny will have about an hour to carry the body into the ruins and return, which will use up Caster's remaining shards. Sunny knows he is stressing how much he owes him. Caster says to act natural, and since Harper has been in the castle until recently, no one will notice his absence soon. When Sunny wonders how many bodies Caster has hidden, Caster says this is his first, since in the Dark City it is usually better to leave bodies in plain sight.

Back at the lodge, Sunny falls asleep at once, and in the morning no one notices anything. He is disturbed that someone could die so utterly unnoticed, which is how he has always imagined his own death. He spends the day in his room, and trains only briefly, noticing Nephis frowning at his sword work before someone calls her away. He is angry, and wonders why his mind feels like it did on the Ashen Barrow.

Cassie is waiting in his room, holding her staff, with a forced smile. She says she has a present, and a spark passes from her to him: the Spell announces he has received the Memory Endless Spring. She says she just wanted to give it to him after everything he has done for them. She holds his shoulder for a strangely long time and says they will meet again soon. At the door she freezes and says quietly, without turning, 'Goodbye, Sunny.'

For the rest of the day Sunny counts hours until sunset, when he must retrieve Harper's body and carry it into the ruins. People rarely leave the hill after dark, because any light attracts creatures no human wants to meet. He does not need light and knows the area well from Effie's lessons, but his heart feels colder with each minute. As the Crimson Spire's shadow falls, Nephis appears at his door and says, 'Come with me.' He fears Caster has told her everything.

She leads him to a remote alley in the red light of sunset and says that she saw him practicing with the sword today, and that his movements were weak and aimless, as if he had lost all clarity. She asks what he was thinking about. He feels relief that she does not know, but also anger, and says murder. He reminds her that she told him the essence of combat is murder, and asks how she knows so much about it, since the day she cut off Andel's head without batting an eye, and while preaching that we are all human and not beasts. Was Andel not human?

Nephis says it is not that she has murdered many people, but that many have tried to murder her. Her family was powerful, and power creates enemies who remain after it disappears. The first time someone tried to kill her she was five or six: her nanny led her to an empty room and tried to strangle her, and she thought it was a game. That was how she learned what weakness is, and when her teacher happened by and killed the nanny with his Aspect Ability, she learned what strength is. Sunny realizes that Nephis too knows powerlessness. She says she has seen how he stared at her since the Spire Messenger and asks him to come clean. He says he wants to know what her real goal is, and whether it is all worth it.

Nephis is surprised by the question and says her goal is obvious: she is trying to help these people. Sunny asks if he has ever told her about his sister, and tells it. After their parents died, his sister was adopted and he ended up on the streets, imagining her life was as bitter as his. He became obsessed with finding her, saving her, and becoming a family again. City databases were sealed to someone like him, so he saved every credit he earned from horrid jobs, even when he barely ate. After four or five years, when he was nearly seventeen, he had enough to hire a detective who sometimes paid street kids for information. A month later the detective gave him a paper with an address.

He went there, and saw a girl around twelve in a tidy school uniform near the tram terminal, and did not realize it was his sister until she entered the house at the address. It was dark and raining, and the house was in a nice district, with a lawn and a big window shining light. Standing in the shadows outside the light, he watched through the window like a television show. She had loving parents, real food, pretty clothes, expensive textbooks, cute younger siblings, and everyone was laughing. He looked at his ragged clothes, bruised knuckles, and frail body, and understood that she never needed him, probably did not remember him, and that returning would only make things worse. Something inside him died in the dark. He turned away, and a few days later began showing the first symptoms of the Nightmare Spell.

He says it was the only selfless thing he has ever done, because even a cretin like him realized the person he wanted to save did not need saving, and asks why Nephis, with all her intelligence, cannot do the same. She says she is not lying about wanting to help. He says he does not buy her savior act, and asks what she is going to help them with, becoming corpses. He reminds her of Cassie's vision of fire and rivers of blood, and asks if that is her plan. For the first time there is a burning emotion in her eyes. After a moment she says, 'Fine. You got me.'

Sunny is stunned that she admits it so easily. Nephis shrugs and says he is the one obsessed with lies. She thanks him, because she had a sheltered upbringing and knew little about communicating with others. She says no one survives in the Dream Realm alone, so she watched Cassie and Sunny and tried to learn, and noticed that nothing Sunny ever said or did was true, since he always hid his real thoughts, desires, and reasons. She calls his mind games almost as devious as the Soul Devourer's hex, and says she never knew you could turn truths into lies. While he learned swordsmanship from her, she learned how to use people from him. She asks where he gets the audacity to blame her for doing what he does to everyone, since she has not told one lie to these people, only given them enough truth to deceive themselves.

Sunny trembles at the thought that she learned from him. She says that if he wants the whole truth, there will be fire and rivers of blood, and she will kill Gunlaug. The castle will fall into civil war among the five lieutenants, and she will kill them too. When she is the last one standing, she will gather the survivors and make a road of bones for the lucky few to reach the Gateway, a chance to return or die standing with a sword in hand instead of living like rats.

Sunny realizes that he is judging from his old viewpoint of survival at all costs, while she taught him that some things are worth more than staying alive. But who gave her the right to decide for others? He asks if Gunlaug is so bad. She says she will not judge him for the despicable things, since keeping a thousand hopeless people alive in this hell could turn a saint into a demon. Her only unforgivable charge is that he gave up and never tried to reach the Gateway, abandoning his duty as an Awakened and submitting to the Spell. Sunny sees that this, not his cruelty, enrages her most, which may be the key to her goal. He asks how many people she is ready to sacrifice. Without a shadow of doubt, she says, 'All of them. Of course.'

Sunny feels a terrible headache as the sun nearly sets. He asks what can be important enough to condemn everyone to death. He guesses glory for the Immortal Flame clan, a duty or oath to be the first human to conquer the Fourth Nightmare as her father conquered the Third and her grandfather the Second, or something worse, saving the world. Nephis grins, with the same maniacal glimmer he saw when he said Aster, Song, Vale, and says she is not going to save the world. White flames ignite in her eyes: 'I'm going to destroy it.' She means the Dream Realm. She will be the first to conquer every Nightmare, destroying anything in her way, and when she reaches the heart of the Nightmare Spell, she will obliterate it. Gunlaug, a Fallen Terror, and the three ghouls cannot stop her, and anyone who dares will die.

Sunny steps back and asks why she wants to destroy the Spell. She says simply, 'Because I hate it.' She does things because she wants to, and he calls her insane. She says that in a world gone mad, she would be wary of anyone who stayed sane. She asks if he has more questions before the sun is gone. He says no, and walks away saying he has an errand. She tells him to come back, but he disappears into the shadows.

Later he walks through the ruins with Harper's body on his shoulder, light because the young man was so gaunt. His heart and mind are empty, and he focuses on not stumbling on a monster, since he feels guilty but not enough to die disposing of the body. He finds a partly collapsed house far into the ruins, throws the corpse in, and looks back at the hill. Hundreds of people are sleeping there, and most of them will die. He sees his future: watching Nephis build her sect, helping defend her from Gunlaug, going on hunts, staying invisible, afraid to get close to anyone, until it all ends in bloodshed, with Caster waiting to use his leverage. He stands a long time looking at the lone glimmer of human light in the darkness, then turns his back and walks into the dark.

Three months later, Sunny is back at the castle. He returned once before to buy a few hard-to-find items, when Nephis's cohort was away on a hunt, but not today. Hearing Changing Star's voice, he turns and says, 'Hey, Neph. Long time no see,' with a slight tremble. Nephis looks more radiant than ever in pristine white armor with clean combed silver hair. He looks like a pile of dirt that came to life, and the Puppeteer's Shroud has seen better days. He does not want her to think he has been miserable, since he lives in a palace, eats well, and is rich. He realizes he said 'Why did she have to be here' out loud. She says it was not polite, but she is glad to see him alive. He asks if she did not expect him to survive without her, and she says on the contrary, because a cockroach like him is not easy to kill. She says she meant it as a compliment.

He is glad to see her too, and has missed her calm presence, but nothing has changed after their quarrel, and the future Cassie foretold is still inevitable. He sees that she looks stronger, with a presence that has grown to a new level, and that months of hunting alone in the dark have made him stronger, smarter, more deadly, and a little insane. She asks what brings him to the castle, and he blurts that he is shopping, saying aloud that he has shards and wants to buy some Memories. His shadow laughs at him. She asks if they can go somewhere to talk, and he refuses, saying he is waiting for someone, an associate.

An enchanting voice calls from the alley entrance: 'Sunny? Hey, are you here?' Kai enters in burnished brown leather and blue silk, with a bright smile. Sunny turns, relieved, but sees that Nephis has taken a step back. Her face is pale and her eyes wide and glassy, consumed by what looks like absolute, utter horror.

Sunny has never seen Nephis afraid. He tenses and holds out a hand ready to summon the Midnight Shard, wondering if Kai is some primordial evil after all. But Kai just looks confused, and Sunny has seen people greet him warmly, so he cannot be a Nightmare Creature. Nephis whispers, 'What is Night doing here?' and clarifies that she means here, on the Forgotten Shore. Sunny asks if they knew each other in the real world. She asks, 'You don't know who he is?' Kai says that he really doesn't, and that it is wonderful. Nephis whispers that Night from Nightingale is the best and most famous idol group of the last decade, with three Orpheus awards, a hundred consecutive weeks at the top of all charts, and six diamond albums, and he is the lead vocalist.

Sunny realizes that Nephis is not horrified, but starstruck. He bursts out laughing, remembering her headphones, and that mighty Changing Star was brought down by a dainty idol boy. Kai and Nephis glare. Sunny says Night has been here for two and a half years and lives in the castle. Nephis says she thought the group was on hiatus because of a solo project by Gale. Kai apologizes, saying he has indeed been here all this time, and that his agency probably invented a cover story, since he is not technically dead or even Hollow, just asleep.

Kai says it is nice to meet another friend of Sunny's and asks her name. Sunny introduces Nephis, adding that she goes by another name these days: Changing Star of the Immortal Flame clan. Kai stares with horror for a moment, but hides it quickly thanks to idol training, and says it is an honor. Nephis turns toward the wall, blushing a little, and says Sunny's friend is here, so can they talk now. She adds that it is something important, a matter of life and death.

A matter of life and death from Nephis is serious, but she is also not to be trusted. Sunny knows the true face of Changing Star now, and the endless force of her conviction. In her inferno, human concepts like loyalty, mercy, and affection are reduced to ash, and if push came to shove she would sacrifice anything or anyone for her goal, including him. Something is also different in how she looks at him, and he doubts trust can be put back once broken. Yet he cannot refuse her. She is still one of the only two people he cares about, and the feeling is like a second Flaw that has taken root and grown stronger in their absence. He is being pulled back into the mess of humanity, which is why he was reluctant to return. But he will not be her compliant sidekick, and will deal on his own terms.

He tells her they can talk, but later, when he has finished his business, since she cannot have expected him to show up today. She says he knows where to go. He adds that he is bringing Night along. Both stare in doubt, and he pretends surprise that Kai does not want to meet his other friends, who can answer his stupid questions. Truthfully, he does not trust the archer either, but his ability to detect lies will be handy in a talk with Nephis, the one graduate of his school of deception.

He pushes Kai away and asks what he found out about Memories. They enter the castle, as the guest of a well-regarded resident this time. The Guards glance with disdain but do nothing, and at Harper's desk sits a similarly downtrodden young woman. The world did not care about one little human dying, he thinks. Kai says he did better and got an invitation to the Memory Market, where Memories can be bought, usually only open to the Host. He leads Sunny through forbidden corridors and down stairs to a wooden door marked with a sword and shield, winks, and opens it.

Behind the door is a medium-sized windowless hall lit by a levitating lantern. Along the walls are weapon racks, wooden mannequins in full armor, and tables of beautiful objects, all Memories, even the lantern. Sunny thinks only of how much money it is, a fortune rivaling a corporation. Kai introduces Stev, who runs the market, a man nearing twenty-five, old by Dark City standards, tall with a round face and cheerful eyes, and obese, the first fat person Sunny has met there. Stev calls him a dirty vagrant, and Sunny calls him a fat bastard and asks if he is sure the vagrant will not break every bone in his blob of a body. After a silence Stev laughs thunderously and says he lacks entertainment.

Stev says a good Memory costs at least a dozen shards. Sunny says he has never absorbed a single soul shard, which Kai, who detects lies, knows is true. Sunny says it on purpose, so that Kai will not question how much he spends, and says Kai will hand over the shards while he picks the right Memories, since he has an eye for them, which really means that his eyes can read their true weave. Stev says Kai could have just asked him, since he cannot lie to Night. Kai whispers that the favor Sunny wanted was to pretend to buy a Memory for him to keep a hidden ace. Sunny says no, he wants him to buy around ten.

He walks among the roughly hundred Memories: swords, daggers, polearms, axes, hammers, bows, armors of every kind, and tables of objects. Touching them reveals their weave, and he sorts the good from the borderline awful. The awful ones are what he came for, since quantity matters, not quality. He is almost done choosing the worst when he sees a dusty, seemingly discarded suit of armor in a badly lit corner, and his hands tremble.

Sunny freezes for a moment, then acts as before, since the first rule of haggling is never to show interest. Judging by the neglect, Stev does not know its true value, and Sunny wants to keep it that way. The jet-black suit of ancient plate has an intricate, solemn design, radiating dark resolve and adamantine grace. It is almost identical to the Stone Saint's armor, but more impressive, as if it belonged to a creature of higher status, and cut from pure black onyx instead of granite. Sunny walks past, then casually puts his hand on its breastplate. His pupils widen. Its weave of diamond strings is far more complex than the Puppeteer's Shroud's, connected by six large, bright embers: a sixth-tier Ascended Memory, the kind only a Fallen Terror leaves behind. 'Jackpot.'

But thousands of strings are torn and floating free, so the pattern has no logic or purpose. A damaged Memory should repair itself in the Soul Sea unless it is completely destroyed, and he has an idea why it does not. Stev chuckles and puts a giant hand on his shoulder, calling it an awesome armor. Sunny says it is by far the most outrageous piece of crap in the market. Stev agrees it is useless. It was here before he took charge and he treats it as a mascot. It is made of actual stone, so heavy that not even Tessai could move in it, and it is not that hard. It once belonged to a member of the cohort that conquered the castle, some say the first Lord himself, and supposedly had an enchantment that made it lighter. When fighting an ancient terror, perhaps the Spire Messenger, it was damaged, and the enchantment broke. It is so damaged that the Spell calls it unknown in every way.

Sunny thinks that the Stone Saint was supposedly made by one of the Unknown, so her kind's armaments might be too. He understands why the armor stays dormant, and it has to do with the difference between Sleepers and Awakened.

Sunny reasons that Awakened can channel soul essence, which Sleepers cannot, and that is vital to unlocking the full power of higher-rank Memories. It is why Legacy clans do not simply arm their scions with great weapons, and even Gunlaug mostly uses his armor for its durability and one passive enchantment. The onyx armor, like the Stone Saint's, is a living armament, a dead stone when its main enchantment is inactive. After being damaged it must be awakened with soul essence to repair itself, but no human on the Shore can channel it, so it remains broken and useless. He does not care that it is damaged, since it has six Ascended embers for his Stone Saint to devour, and she might gain something extra because of their shared origin. He briefly wonders if she might refuse to destroy it, then dismisses it. He calls it tacky decoration, and walks away.

Ten minutes later he hands Kai a rucksack and names the Memories to buy. Kai asks if he was serious about ten and whether he knows how much Memories cost. Sunny tells him to open the rucksack. Inside are about seventy soul shards, more than most people in the Dark City will see in their lifetime, enough to start a bloody conflict. Kai asks where he got them, and Sunny says they were gathering dust in his bedroom. Kai asks if he really lives in that cathedral, and whether there is really a Fallen Devil there. Sunny says yes, and Kai stares at the wall like a man who has realized nothing makes sense.

Kai names the ten worst Memories in Stev's inventory, including the damaged onyx armor. Stev turns green and begs him to reconsider, saying they are trash. Sunny says one man's trash is another man's treasure, and says Stev admitted they are the worst, so there should be a big discount. In an empty corridor, Kai takes Sunny's hand, and sparks pass between them. The Spell announces 'You have received a Memory…' ten times. Sunny has bought ten Memories for his Shadow, including the tier-six Ascended armor for seven soul shards. He grins, then it fades and something dark glints in his eyes. It is time to talk to Nephis.

On the way out, Kai is quiet. Sunny thinks about the lodge, and briefly considers rushing back to his cathedral without keeping his promise, but resolves to pretend he does not care and demand compensation for whatever Nephis wants, since he is an outsider now and his services will not be cheap. There is one thing he wants to do but cannot alone, and maybe the cohort could help. Kai asks why he wanted him to come, and Sunny says to tell him if he is being lied to. Kai asks why he is wary of Lady Nephis, and Sunny says she is the kind of friend you do not lower your guard around. There is also Caster, whom he especially distrusts. Kai has heard only good things, and Sunny says he gives him the creeps. Caster has done nothing to deserve hostility, but he is too perfect, and in Sunny's experience only people with bad intentions look that flawless.

The lodge has grown, with extra structures, fortified on the side facing the white road, lookouts with bows on the roof, and tasteful interiors with carpets and tapestries. It is the largest building in the settlement, almost a small town hall, and people have lost the rot of hopelessness. Sunny wonders why Gunlaug has not put an end to it. A young woman greets them, and asks who Neph is, and he has to say Lady Nephis, Changing Star of the Immortal Flame clan. On the way he passes his old room and sees Caster's belongings in it.

The old central hall is now a walled room with a wide window onto the city, a dense map, and a table with seven chairs. Effie sits with her feet on the table, and Cassie holds a cup. Nephis and Caster stand at the map. Sunny grins and introduces Kai. Kai greets Nephis, Cassie, Caster, and Huntress Athena. Cassie says she thought she heard Night from Nightingale say her name, and Kai says he is. Her face goes deathly pale, her hands tremble, and she drops the cup, which Effie catches, sighing that it happens every time. Sunny thinks that the reaction was unnecessary.
